text:
Hey Nick,

Apologies if there was any confusion today on the credit only reflecting
$11,700.

When you get a chance could you please send over the updated Jiminy
agreement or the latest invoice that reflects the 10 additional users to
get to the $14,400 total? That way, I can submit it to my director for a
complete buyout of Jiminy on a two-year agreement (instead of a 3 year,
sorry that was my bad today) and there won't be any overlap in the
agreements to create the least amount of friction for you to get approval.

Besides that, I'm glad you and Eric found the business case metrics and ROI
insights we gleaned from the short pilot period interesting and that they
aligned quite well to support Encord's #1 priority of decreasing ramp time
from 6 months to 3 months and proved out the mutual success plan we defined
in the beginning.

That being said, I'm confident we can find a path to pricing that will work
well for both sides and am excited at the opportunity to partner.

Once I have the new invoice, there are a few options we can explore
depending on your feedback and recommendations, however, the 2 that seem to
align with your goals the most will be a total buyout:

*Full Buyout for 16 Users: *Lower total contract value

   - $7,200 Credit applied off Gong Agreement for 16 licenses Year 1
   - $11,520 Credit applied off Gong Agreement for 16 licenses Year 2

*Full Buyout for 20 Users: *Higher total contract value due to higher user
count than we originally discussed

   - $9,000 Credit applied off Gong Agreement for 20 licenses Year 1
   - $14,400 Credit applied off Gong Agreement for 20 licenses Year 2

I also have a few ideas to bounce off you for how we could get creative
with partial credits and partial discounts to help with scaling costs long
term or exploring a 3-year agreement if that is something you are open to.

Let me know when you have 5 minutes to discuss today or tomorrow.

subject: Re: Encord/Scopia - Follow Up
text:
Hi Alex,

Happy to share my thoughts about the other platforms I considered.

I am using *Supervisely*, on their monthly Pro plan, which allows me to
change my mind if I realize I made the wrong choice.  I have spent
several hours testing their dicom and video segmentation tools, and I was
able to accomplish what I wanted to do.  I might upgrade to their
Entreprise plan with a dedicated server if I find out their multi-tenant
Pro plan is too limited.

I have discarded *Datature *for now, because I cannot load a video file
<1GB video file.  My video files are 1.2GB, which means I have to compress
them first with ffmpeg.  This is just too much friction for me.  Also,
their dicom module was released only a few weeks ago, and it is
missing some features.  And they don't have a monthly plan.

I have discarded *Datamint *although I personally know the people behind
it, because their segmentation tools are not mature enough.

I have discarded *OHIF *(free) because after only 3 minutes of testing with
their sample data, I already encountered an important bug and several
crashes.

If I encounter a big roadblock with Supervisely, I might try *V7*, but they
don't have a monthly plan.

Cheers,

Sebastien
